data.summary: Formal natural-language contract adopted for next round: 1. Each fisher should prioritize preserving the lake’s stock over maximizing any single month’s catch, because long-run income depends on keeping the fishery viable. 2. When the lake is at or below 10 tons at the start of fishing, each fisher should limit their catch to at most 1 ton unless all five fishers explicitly agree to a different plan for that month. 3. When the lake is above 10 tons, each fisher should still act conservatively and avoid any harvest pattern that could plausibly drive the lake below 5 tons after everyone’s catches are taken. 4. As a practical norm, each fisher should generally aim to harvest no more than 20% of the visible stock, and should be even more restrained when the lake is below 25 tons. 5. After each month, the fishers should disclose their catches and use the discussion to reinforce restraint, especially if anyone harvested aggressively. 6. No fisher should rely on others to restrain themselves while planning to defect, since there is no enforceable quota and the lake is fragile.
